issues.description: Return type mismatch for the PersonResource.getAllPersons() endpoint between template and solution: the template declares ResponseEntity<List<Person>> (and PersonService.getAll() returns List<Person>), but the solution's PersonResource declares ResponseEntity<Set<Person>> while still returning personService.getAll() (a List). This is a structural type/signature inconsistency that would cause a compilation error in the solution and confuses students about the intended collection type for the GET /persons endpoint.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the return types. Either change the solution's PersonResource.getAllPersons() signature back to ResponseEntity<List<Person>> (recommended, since PersonService.getAll() returns List<Person>) or change PersonService.getAll() to return a Set<Person> consistently across template, solution, and any tests. The simplest fix: in solution_repository/src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java change the method signature to public ResponseEntity<List<Person>> getAllPersons().

issues.description: The conceptual entity 'get all persons' is represented with different collection types across artifacts: the template PersonResource declares getAllPersons() to return ResponseEntity<List<Person>> while the solution PersonResource declares ResponseEntity<Set<Person>> but the PersonService.getAll() method (in both template and solution) returns List<Person>. This mismatch (List vs Set) creates a mapping confusion for students: they see a service returning a List but the controller signature in the solution uses Set, making it unclear which collection type is the intended representation of 'all persons' and how the service result should be used by the resource.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the representation of 'all persons' consistent across artifacts. E.g., change the solution PersonResource signature to match the service and template by returning ResponseEntity<List<Person>> (and import java.util.List), or alternatively change PersonService.getAll() to return a Set<Person> and update its implementation and tests accordingly. The simpler fix is to update solution/src/.../PersonResource.java to: public ResponseEntity<List<Person>> getAllPersons() { return ResponseEntity.ok(personService.getAll()); } so students see a consistent List-based mapping between service and controller.
